# Graph operations · sim

Ports, defaults, and constraints come from the registered operations. Use `graph describe <op> --json` for the full structured record.

### sim.controller

Replay a controller from timed target and measurement samples.

Origin: toolkit.

| Direction | Port | Type | Default | Details |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `controller` | `record` | Required | {"layout":"Plain named object"} |
| Input | `samples` | `array<record>` | Required | {"items":"record"} |
| Input | `options` | `record` | `{}` | {"layout":"Plain named object"} |
| Input | `checkpoint` | `record` | `{}` | {"layout":"Plain named object"} |
| Output | `value` | `record` | — | {"layout":"Plain named object"} |
| Output | `checkpoint` | `record` | — | {"layout":"Plain named object"} |

Guides: [guide](../controllers-inverse-targets.md#author-a-controller)

Get the runnable example with `ink-studio graph describe sim.controller --example > example.json`.
Run it with `ink-studio graph run example.json`.

### sim.mpm

Sample an MPM recipe with per-material coverage, density, compression and measured obstacle contact.

Origin: toolkit.
Samples the graph clock.

| Direction | Port | Type | Default | Details |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `recipe` | `record` | `{}` | {"layout":"Plain named object"} |
| Input | `checkpoint` | `record` | `{}` | {"layout":"Plain named object"} |
| Input | `options` | `record` | `{}` | {"layout":"Plain named object"} |
| Output | `value` | `raster` | — | {"layout":"Interleaved samples on a positive integer grid","channels":[1,4],"finite":true} |
| Output | `field` | `raster` | — | {"layout":"Interleaved samples on a positive integer grid","channels":[1,4],"finite":true} |
| Output | `points` | `array<record>` | — | {"items":"record"} |
| Output | `checkpoint` | `record` | — | {"layout":"Plain named object"} |
| Output | `report` | `record` | — | {"layout":"Plain named object"} |
| Output | `grid` | `gridField` | — | {"layout":"One to three sampled axes, X-fastest, with origin, spacing and interleaved components"} |
| Output | `pointBuffer` | `pointBuffer` | — | {"layout":"Packed XYZ positions, optional IDs and velocities, with coordinate frame and unit"} |
| Output | `materialCoverage` | `array<raster>` | — | coverage ratio · {"items":"raster"} |
| Output | `materialDensity` | `array<raster>` | — | relative mass per art pixel · {"items":"raster"} |
| Output | `materialCompression` | `array<raster>` | — | local area contraction ratio · {"items":"raster"} |
| Output | `compression` | `raster` | — | local area contraction ratio · {"layout":"Interleaved samples on a positive integer grid","channels":[1,4],"finite":true} |
| Output | `contact` | `raster` | — | relative mass × art pixels per second · {"layout":"Interleaved samples on a positive integer grid","channels":[1,4],"finite":true} |
| Output | `collisionMask` | `raster` | — | byte coverage · {"layout":"Interleaved samples on a positive integer grid","channels":[1,4],"finite":true} |

- Use an mpm recipe or matching checkpoint. Material arrays are ordered by the recipe materials.
- Contact accumulates collision momentum corrections across the most recent tick. It clears on the next tick.
- Use raster.select to route one material plane into a downstream node.

Guides: [guide](../headless-authoring.md#planar-simulation-recipes), [guide](../material-point-impacts.md)

Get the runnable example with `ink-studio graph describe sim.mpm --example > example.json`.
Run it with `ink-studio graph run example.json`.
